summary: Vericiguat is an oral soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC) stimulator used to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization in adults with symptomatic chronic heart failure and ejection fraction below 45% following a worsening event (recent HF hospitalization or outpatient IV diuretic). It is started at 2.5 mg once daily with food and doubled about every 2 weeks to the target of 10 mg once daily as tolerated. It carries a boxed warning for embryo-fetal toxicity and is contraindicated in pregnancy and with other sGC stimulators. The main adverse effect is hypotension.
indications: To reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization in adults with symptomatic chronic heart failure and ejection fraction less than 45% following a hospitalization for heart failure or need for outpatient intravenous diuretics

dosage.d: 2.5 mg orally once daily with food
dosage.n: Take with food to optimize absorption

dosage.d: Double the dose to 5 mg, then 10 mg, approximately every 2 weeks as tolerated
dosage.n: Titrate based on blood pressure and tolerability

dosage.d: Consider reducing to the previously tolerated dose if symptomatic low BP or SBP <90 mmHg
Tablets may be crushed and mixed with water for patients unable to swallow whole

admin: If a dose is missed, take as soon as remembered on the same day; do not double up the next day
Tablets may be crushed and mixed with water immediately before administration if swallowing is difficult
Check seated/standing blood pressure during titration
Do not co-administer with other sGC stimulators such as riociguat or with PDE5 inhibitors
moa: Vericiguat is a stimulator of soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC), an important enzyme in the nitric oxide (NO) signaling pathway. In heart failure, impaired NO synthesis and reduced sGC activity contribute to myocardial and vascular dysfunction. Vericiguat directly stimulates sGC independently of NO and also acts synergistically with available NO to increase intracellular cyclic GMP, leading to smooth muscle relaxation and vasodilation, with beneficial effects on cardiac and vascular function.

absolute: Concomitant use with other soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators (e.g., riociguat)
relative: Symptomatic hypotension or SBP <100 mmHg at initiation
monitor: Pregnancy status in females of reproductive potential

preg: Boxed warning: vericiguat may cause fetal harm and is contraindicated in pregnancy. Verify pregnancy status before starting. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for one month after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on the presence of vericiguat in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise patients not to breastfeed during treatment.
renal: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild to moderate renal impairment. Vericiguat has not been studied in patients with eGFR less than 15 mL/min/1.73 m2 at initiation or those on dialysis, so use is not recommended in these patients.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed in mild to moderate hepatic impairment. Vericiguat has not been studied in severe (Child-Pugh C) hepatic impairment and is not recommended in these patients.

major: Other sGC stimulators (riociguat) - contraindicated; additive hypotension
PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil) - additive hypotension; concomitant use not recommended
moderate: Other antihypertensives, nitrates, diuretics - additive blood-pressure-lowering effect
Alcohol in large amounts - additive hypotension
minor: No clinically significant CYP-mediated interactions; metabolized mainly by glucuronidation
interactions.food: Take with food; food increases bioavailability by about 44% and reduces variability.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction, but may add to blood-pressure lowering and dizziness.
interactions.diagnostics: May lower hemoglobin (anemia reported); monitor as clinically indicated.

emergency: Severe symptomatic hypotension with end-organ hypoperfusion

monitoring: Blood pressure at baseline and during dose titration
Pregnancy status before initiation in females of reproductive potential
Heart failure symptoms and functional status
Renal and hepatic function as clinically indicated
counsel: Take once daily with food at about the same time each day
This medicine can cause low blood pressure - rise slowly and report dizziness or fainting
Do not take with riociguat or erectile dysfunction drugs (PDE5 inhibitors) unless your doctor approves
If you can become pregnant, use effective birth control during and for 1 month after stopping; tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant
Do not stop your other heart failure medicines unless instructed
pk: Pharmacologic effect within hours of dosing
Tmax approximately 1 hour (fasted) to 4 hours (with food)
Approximately 30 hours in patients with heart failure
Supports once-daily dosing; steady state in about 6 days
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C
pearls: Boxed warning: embryo-fetal toxicity - contraindicated in pregnancy
Used on top of (not instead of) guideline-directed HFrEF therapy after a worsening event
Take with food - increases bioavailability by ~44%
Avoid combining with riociguat or PDE5 inhibitors (additive hypotension)
Hypotension and anemia are the principal adverse effects; uptitrate to 10 mg as tolerated
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered on the same day. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed dose; resume the once-daily schedule the next day.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Overdose is most likely to cause hypotension. Provide supportive cardiovascular care and standard measures to support blood pressure. Because of high (~98%) plasma protein binding, vericiguat is not expected to be removed by dialysis.
